scope: Bounded read-only comparison of source equations with current profile-drag, stall and fast/current implementations. This is a source review, not numerical verification or ASWING equivalence.

findings.finding: The current path constructs separate control-point and bound-vortex influence operators. Lift and section normal speed use bound-vortex relative velocity, including freestream, rotational reference velocity, gust, local motion, volume flow and jets; own bound filament is excluded before summation. This agrees with steady Eq67 and the Vperp definition. The broad unsteady physical-quarter-chord position mapping needs separate geometry review, not a profile-drag substitution.

Friction uses .5 rho |V_hv| V_hv c Cdf; pressure uses .5 rho |V_hv_perp| V_hv_perp c Cdp; separated-flow drag uses 2 rho V_hv_perp/|V_hv_perp| times the squared CP normal tangency times c. Each is integrated with current interval length. Equation70 marks only the normal-velocity square as CP-evaluated; replacing all V/Vperp by CP values is not supported by this source.

cl=2 Gamma/(chord Vperp) and leakage=(Vperp/dCLda) Ks fstall agree algebraically because 4 pi h=dCLda. The residual subtracts leakage from CP normal velocity. Its Jacobian differentiates both lift coefficient and bound normal speed.

The sorted/log1p/expit/expm1 implementation is an algebraically stable evaluation of delta_cl[log(1+exp((cl-clmax)/delta_cl))-log(1+exp((clmin-cl)/delta_cl))]. The derivative is the sum of the two sigmoid terms. The threshold 32 switches evaluation formula, not the constitutive law. No output clipping or decreasing poststall circulation is introduced.

Ks=40 and delta_cl=.05 agree with approximate values recommended in the public theory. They are exposed parameters and do not modify the literal ±1.2 section limits. Neither the original SA1 model nor its script records these build constants, so exact ASWING 5.96 defaults remain unproved. Changing them to improve agreement would be a fit, not a confirmed source correction.

The section moment uses the physical quarter-chord arm along c_hat, cross circulatory lift, plus .5 rho Vperp² c² Cm s_hat; local normal Mach scales Cm independently of the PG matrix setting. There is no extra local profile-drag couple, consistent with Eq74. Global force transport remains about the literal reference point. SA1 literal section Cm is 0, but its lift-arm contribution and exported CM remain required.

The CP normal velocity receives the documented 2/pi circulation-rate lag correction before separation drag. Rate lift uses the documented rho c Gamma_dot/Vperp cross V,s factor. Beam-axis velocity is separately used for apparent-mass terms. In steady SA1, rates, local motion and circulation-rate terms are zero; substituting an axis velocity into steady profile drag is not a supported correction.

The fast branch caches undeformed geometry influence coefficients with zero wind angles; the current branch uses current wind direction and geometry. Current circulation, section properties, frames, kinematics, loads and independently chosen Mach remain active. This agrees with K/F for the rigid steady SA1 scope. Frozen cache keys include Mach/core/ground metadata. The script F toggle and unknown startup state remain a setup qualification, not a reason to choose the closer branch.

Steady Eq155 places the virtual bound-vortex receiver using the wind-aligned quarter-chord construction; unsteady Eq29 names the physical quarter-chord arm along the section c-axis. Current steady geometry uses Eq155 while moment transfer uses the physical arm. A full moving-section interpretation requires the separate geometry/API audit. It is not evidence that the steady SA1 profile velocities should be replaced or fitted.
